Subject: Session affinity & commitment roadmap for dedicated fleet

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Avery liked the latency profiles and the ability to route to regional capacity. We are starting to scope a dedicated deployment and need a short pre-sales sizing pass so we can align procurement and engineering. High level context: 
- Customer: Avery Technologies (SaaS for financial planning chatbots)
- Expected launch: Q4 2026 (pilot in Aug)
- Usage pattern: heavy day-time burst with several short tail spikes around earnings reports; global users but US-heavy initially

Quick answers we can share now:
- Concurrent sessions: ~1,200 sustained; peaks to ~9,000 during 10–15 minute burst windows (market opens)
- Average prompt length: 45 tokens; average generation: 220 tokens; some multimodal prompts from internal tools up to 700 tokens occasionally
- Session behavior: users maintain conversational sessions with an average of 6 turns; we do want session affinity (sticky KV cache per user) to reduce cold starts

Can you send a short questionnaire or checklist (concurrency, token mixes, tail-latency targets, pre-warm strategies) so we can finish our internal sizing and budget ask? Attaching a sample session_profile.csv exported from our telemetry.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Head of Platform Ops
Avery Technologies

Priya —

Appreciate the telemetry snapshot, that helps a lot. I attached a 6‑question quick intake below that will let us produce a conservative committed-capacity recommendation and an alternative burstable topology. Short asks:

1) Do you expect KV (per-session) cache to be warm across turns (i.e., same encoder context reused) or do users frequently start fresh?
2) P99 latency target for generation (ms)? Is 350ms acceptable for your customer SLAs during bursts?
3) Any hard limits on cost per 1k tokens for pilot vs GA?
4) Are you planning on pinning a single model family (e.g., Llama 2 x.x variants) or allowing model fallbacks during high load?
5) Will user sessions be spread across regions or are you planning US-only for initial rollout?
6) Any data residency/KMS requirements we should factor into Private deployment options?

If you prefer, we can run a short 45-minute sizing workshop with my team (Vivek + Marissa) and your infra lead.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Priya — quick follow from our infra side. A few clarifying notes so we size correctly: 

- Session affinity: If sessions are sticky and KV cache is warm, effective per-request compute drops substantially (lower token decode+KV overhead). Please confirm if you can persist session affinity for at least 90s between turns.
- Token mix: you listed 45 prompt / 220 generate average. Please confirm 10th/90th percentile for generation length (we often see long tail; 700 occurs occasionally but percentiles will change sizing).
- P99 target: our standard guidance for chat customers on Dedicated is 300–450ms depending on model family and batching. If you need sub-200ms p99 we will recommend higher commit tiers or smaller sequence-optimized model variants.
- Warm pool/pre-warm: For your 10–15 minute bursts, pre-warm + pooled session workers reduce cold start spikes. Tell us how long you can provide an advance notice TTL for market events (e.g., 5 minutes notice vs none).

I'll attach a short PDF with preliminary SLA/commit tradeoffs and our preferred sizing knobs. We can convert your session_profile.csv into a draft occupancy heatmap in the workshop.

—Vivek
VP, Dedicated Products | Redwood Inference

Hi team — adding a short sizing matrix based on the numbers you shared. I converted the CSV and ran a micro-occupancy hypothesis; below are conservative / optimistic rows we typically present to procurement.

Conservative (avoid burst failures):
- Sustained concurrency: 1,200 sessions
- Peak concurrency (15m window): 9,000 sessions
- Avg token mix: 45 in / 220 out (90th gen = 620 tokens)
- Recommended commit: 160 A100-class-equivalent GPUs (or 200x T4-equivalents for cost-saving but higher variance)
- Buffering & pre-warm: pre-warm pool equal to 12% of peak sessions, 5-minute prewarm window recommended for market events

Optimistic (with aggressive KV cache):
- Sustained concurrency: 1,200 sessions
- Peak concurrency: 6,000 sessions (if 85% cache hit rate)
- Recommended commit: 110 A100-class-equivalent GPUs
- Autoscale burst to additional shared capacity for >2x peaks

Questions for Priya (we'll use these in the workshop):
- Can you provide 90th/99th percentiles for generation length? (we need to know tail mass beyond that 700 token example)
- Can Avery send a 48-hour telemetry export with per-minute concurrency? That helps our occupancy simulator produce a per-hour commit recommendation rather than a single-point estimate.
- Any constraint on fallback models during bursts (if you allow smaller quantized variants for bursts we can lower commit significantly)?

I've stubbed a GPU SKU recommendation workbook — attaching gpu_sku_recommendation.xlsx. If you want, I'll run a short simulation live in the workshop using your telemetry and show the delta between commit bands.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is very helpful and exactly what procurement wanted to see. Quick answers: 
- KV cache: yes, sessions are sticky; we can maintain affinity for ~120s between turns.
- 90th/99th gen lengths: 90th ~520 tokens; 99th ~980 tokens (those are heavy analytical queries)
- Pre-warm notification: we can provide a 3–5 minute advance signal for scheduled windows; unpredictable market spikes are the bigger concern
- Model fallback: for bursts we are open to quantized fallbacks provided semantic fidelity is acceptable to product; we want to avoid hallucination regressions.
